A. Every reaction speeds up at any temperature

A. A 100 cm³ measuring cylinder
B. A volumetric pipette

B. Ink could produce additional spots
C. Ink stays fixed while the samples move
D. The baseline must travel with each sample [1]

Part 2: Correct option C (1). C. 0.005 g A negative power of ten represents a fraction: 5/1000 = 0.005 g. Distractor explanations: A: This is 5 × 10⁻⁴ g, ten times too small. B: This is 5 × 10⁻² g, ten times too large. D: This is 5 × 10³ g; the exponent has the wrong sign. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 3: Correct option A (1). A. View the lower meniscus at eye level. Eye-level viewing of the lower meniscus reduces parallax for water. Distractor explanations: B: Water has a concave meniscus; read its lower edge. C: Viewing from below still causes parallax. D: Tilting changes the surface relative to the scale. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 4: Correct option A (1). A. Correcting the offset removes systematic bias A repeated positive zero offset is systematic. Distractor explanations: B: Repeating a fixed offset does not remove systematic error. C: Subtracting the positive offset corrects an over-reading. D: Averaging repeated biased readings retains the offset. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 5: Correct option B (1). B. Gas volume / cm³. The heading names the measured quantity and its volume unit. Distractor explanations: A: Seconds measure time, not volume. Part 6: Correct option C (1). C. kilogram The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram. Distractor explanations: A: The gram is a mass unit but not the SI base unit. B: The newton measures force. D: The mole measures amount of substance. No mark for more than one selected option.
